subject: Cybersecurity
title: Surveillance Capitalism: When Users Are the Product
description: A fast breakdown of Surveillance Capitalism: When Users Are the Product for builders.

hook.text: Google's free services cost you nothing in dollars. You pay with every search, click, location, and conversation.

buildup.text: Surveillance capitalism, coined by Shoshana Zuboff, describes how tech companies extract behavioral data to predict your actions.

discovery.text: Your ‘behavioral surplus’ – data beyond what’s needed for services – is sold to advertisers. Your attention is the real product.

twist.text: Facebook’s internal research showed Instagram harmed teen girls’ mental health. They kept the platform unchanged for profit.

climax.text: The business model of ‘free’ services depends on maximizing data collection. Privacy and profit are fundamentally at odds.

punchline.text: If the product is free, you're what's being sold.

quiz.question: What is 'behavioral surplus' in surveillance capitalism?
options: User data collected beyond what's needed for the service, sold to advertisers
Unused computing power from user devices
